newsitem.title: USA: Stocks soar on economic numbers.
newsitem.headline: Stocks soar on economic numbers.

text.p: Stock prices roared ahead Tuesday on the back of a powerful rally in the bond market after the government reported favourable economic data.
At 10 a.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 80.28 points at 6,863.30.
In the broader market, advancing issues swamped declines by 8 to 2 on active volume of 80 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Financial markets were boosted by news that the Employment Cost Index in the first quarter inched up only 0.6 percent, which was well below the 0.9 percent gain expected by Wall Street.
Also helping sentiment was an unexpected drop of 3.0 percent in durable goods orders in March, the largest drop since August 1996.

The economic reports were welcome news, as they indicated that the economy's growth may be slowing and inflation is still in check -- which should lessen the odds that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates again at its May 20 policy-setting meeting.

In the inflation-sensitive bond market, the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond gained more than a full point, sending its yield down to 7.01 percent from Monday's 7.11 percent. Last Friday the yield was at 7.14 percent.
"I thought it was great. Employment costs are well within confines," said Dick Stein, vice president of U.S. Clearing Corp.

"No one can get upset about that. I think this could get the market moving back to the upside. You could climb from where we closed yesterday," he said. "We could get back to the 6,900 figure between now and the weekend."

Added Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities: "This is a very friendly number. Cause and effect says this is a benign number and bonds are rallying. Bonds are the gatekeeper for stocks. Yesterday the Street made a bet the numbers would be benign and the Street was right."
The Nasdaq Composite Index jumped 16.52 points at 1,233.55.
